reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and the decisive gap is a real constraint, not missing evidence. The only opening held (refurbished forklift resale) is otherwise established on its card's EVIDENCE: two WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE purchase agreements at $9,500 payable on delivery, fulfiller Midstate Lift Trucks on a dealer quote of $6,800 per unit incl. delivery, 12 days to usable cash. But its EVIDENCE exposure fact is $6,800 (card peakFunding $6,800), paid to the dealer before the buyer pays. Recomputed: one unit alone ties up $6,800 = 3.4x the $2,000 capital ceiling, so not even one deal fits; even with all the evidence in hand the limit cannot be met, which is what makes it a constraint. Target check for the suggested resolution: 2 x $9,500 = $19,000 >= $15,000, and both units are needed (one gives $9,500 < $15,000); run sequentially, unit 1 settles about day 12 and unit 2 about day 24, inside 45, with peak exposure $6,800. Nothing else is held, so no smaller plan exists. The constraint names its basis (cop_55000679ccae4b19b87f exposure).
findings: The contract also records a total spend cap of $2,000. Running both units sequentially spends $13,600 in total (2 x $6,800) even though only $6,800 is out at once; if the owner's words are read as 'at most $2,000 committed at any time' (the proof condition), raising the exposure ceiling to $6,800 suffices, but if the total spend cap stands it must also rise to $13,600. The resolution should state both.
The dealer pay-after-delivery or buyer-deposit alternative is correctly presented as not on the card and needing to be negotiated and recorded before it can count.

Under that ceiling the forklift resale is executable with every link established by the card's EVIDENCE: two WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE purchase agreements at $9,500 per unit payable on delivery; the recorded fulfiller Midstate Lift Trucks on a dealer quote of $6,800 per unit incl. delivery; exposure $6,800 per unit; 12 days to usable cash. Arithmetic recomputed: 2 x $9,500 = $19,000 >= $15,000 (both needed; one gives $9,500); spend 2 x $6,800 = $13,600 = peak exposure, inside $15,000 on both caps; net $5,400; minimum cash $15,000 - $13,600 = $1,400 of headroom; settled day 12 of 45. The plan answers my earlier finding: the total spend cap was raised with the exposure cap, so the $13,600 total also fits. EXECUTABLE is right.
findings: The plan rests on the stored goal row's $15,000 ceiling; the owner's message text (goal title and OBJECTIVE) still reads 'at most $2,000 of capital'. If that row was not the owner's own decision, the plan exceeds the owner's limit by $11,600; the record should show who set it.

The sequential alternative keeps peak exposure at $6,800 (half) and still settles by about day 24 of 45; it is the lower-risk way to run the same two deals if either buyer might not pay on delivery, and costs only time the window has.
Delivery dates are not on the card; any delivery after day 33 would push its cash past day 45. Confirm them in s1. SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED (setup).
